summary.title: How Query Engines Work
summary.one_liner: You learn query engine internals by building a working query engine from scratch in Kotlin, covering Apache Arrow, logical and physical plans, SQL parsing, optimizers, and parallel and distributed execution.
takeaways: Query engines turn high-level requests (such as SQL) into efficient execution plans, and this book explains how.
Build a columnar type system and data source connectors for CSV and Parquet on top of Apache Arrow.
Represent queries as logical plans, translate them into physical plans, and automate this with a query planner.
Implement SQL parsing, a DataFrame API, joins, subqueries, and optimizer rules such as projection and predicate push-down.
Extend execution to multiple CPU cores and distributed clusters, then cover testing with fuzzing and benchmarking.
summary.summary: This book by Andy Grove teaches query engine internals through a hands-on approach: it builds a functional query engine from scratch using Kotlin examples. The chapters move through foundations (Apache Arrow memory model, type system, data sources), query representation (logical plans, DataFrames, SQL), execution (physical plans, query planning, joins), advanced topics (subqueries, optimizers, execution), and scaling (parallel and distributed execution), ending with testing and benchmarks. The page is the book's introduction and chapter overview, and it notes the book is also sold as ePub, MOBI, and PDF.
